nodes.name: Email Received
nodes.notes: IMAP IDLE, an outbound connection - no webhook, so nothing has to be reachable. forceReconnect is the floor on latency: IDLE fires when mail ARRIVES, not when a flag changes or when the connection was down, and a reconnect re-runs the UNSEEN search. trackLastMessageId is OFF: the fetch marks a message read BEFORE the uid filter drops it, so a message below the stored uid is marked processed and never processed. UNSEEN alone is the right selector here, because this workflow is what marks mail read.

parameters.query:
-- Find the conversation this reply belongs to.
--
-- Two ways, in this order. The Message-ID we recorded when WF-06 sent is the
-- reliable one: a reply quotes it in In-Reply-To or References. The sender
-- address is the fallback, because a reply can arrive from a colleague the
-- message was forwarded to, or from a different alias of the same person.
--
-- Matching nothing is a normal outcome. This mailbox receives newsletters and
-- service mail too, and those must not reach a classifier or a messages row.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
keys AS (
    SELECT array(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(j -> 'thread_keys') FROM p) AS k,
           (SELECT j ->> 'from_email' FROM p) AS from_email
),
by_thread AS (
    SELECT cv.id AS conversation_id, cv.lead_id
    FROM conversations cv, keys
    WHERE cv.external_thread_id = ANY (keys.k)
    LIMIT 1
),
by_sender AS (
    -- Only a lead we actually wrote to. Someone who has never been contacted
    -- writing in is not a reply to anything.
    SELECT cv.id AS conversation_id, cv.lead_id
    FROM conversations cv
    JOIN leads l  ON l.id = cv.lead_id
    JOIN people pe ON pe.id = l.person_id, keys
    WHERE lower(pe.email) = keys.from_email
    ORDER BY cv.last_message_at DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
),
matched AS (
    SELECT * FROM by_thread
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM by_sender WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM by_thread)
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Exactly one row out, always, matched or not. LEFT JOINs from `p` rather than
-- FROM `matched`, because a node that returns nothing breaks the paired-item
-- lineage back to Prepare Inbound and the branch that handles unmatched mail
-- then reads empty strings for every field. Measured: the first unmatched
-- message produced an alert whose dedup key was the md5 of "".
--
-- The inbound fields are carried back out for the same reason: downstream
-- reads one item rather than reaching across nodes for it.
SELECT m.conversation_id,
       m.lead_id,
       c.id   AS company_id,
       c.name AS company_name,
       pe.full_name,
       pe.email AS lead_email,
       (m.conversation_id IS NOT NULL) AS matched,
       CASE WHEN m.conversation_id IS NULL THEN NULL
            WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM by_thread) THEN 'thread'
            ELSE 'sender' END AS matched_by,
       p.j ->> 'from_email'            AS from_email,
       p.j ->> 'subject'               AS subject,
       p.j ->> 'body'                  AS body,
       p.j ->> 'external_message_id'   AS external_message_id,
       (p.j ->> 'is_auto_reply')::boolean AS is_auto_reply,
       (p.j ->> 'is_bounce')::boolean     AS is_bounce,
       -- A message seen before (a re-activation re-reads the activation day)
       -- must not be classified again or get a second reply draft.
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM messages x
               WHERE x.external_message_id = NULLIF(p.j ->> 'external_message_id', '')) AS already_recorded
FROM p
LEFT JOIN matched m   ON true
LEFT JOIN leads l     ON l.id = m.lead_id
LEFT JOIN companies c ON c.id = l.company_id
LEFT JOIN people pe   ON pe.id = l.person_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ thread_keys: $json.thread_keys, from_email: $json.from_email, subject: $json.subject, body: $json.body, external_message_id: $json.external_message_id, is_auto_reply: $json.is_auto_reply, is_bounce: $json.is_bounce } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- Record the reply and move everything it touches, in one statement.
--
-- Order is the point. prompts/classifier.md: on a stop request the workflow
-- must suppress, cancel unsent outreach, close the conversation and the lead,
-- log it, and never reply - in that order and before anything else. A stop
-- therefore overrides the category entirely: requested_stop on a message the
-- model filed as QUESTION still suppresses.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
c AS (
    SELECT (j ->> 'conversation_id')::uuid           AS conversation_id,
           (j ->> 'lead_id')::uuid                   AS lead_id,
           NULLIF(j ->> 'external_message_id', '')   AS ext_id,
           j ->> 'subject'                           AS subject,
           j ->> 'body'                              AS body,
           lower(j ->> 'from_email')                 AS from_email,
           NULLIF(lower(j ->> 'lead_email'), '')     AS lead_email,
           j #>> '{classification,category}'         AS category,
           (j #>> '{classification,confidence}')::numeric      AS confidence,
           (j #>> '{classification,requested_stop}')::boolean  AS requested_stop,
           (j #>> '{classification,human_required}')::boolean  AS human_required,
           j #>> '{classification,reason}'           AS reason,
           j #>> '{classification,mentioned_timeline}' AS timeline,
           (j ->> 'escalated')::boolean              AS escalated
    FROM p
),
v AS (
    SELECT c.*,
           (c.category = 'UNSUBSCRIBE' OR c.requested_stop) AS is_stop,
           (c.confidence < 0.7)                             AS low_conf
    FROM c
),
msg AS (
    INSERT INTO messages (conversation_id, direction, author, subject, body,
                          classification, classification_confidence,
                          external_message_id, sent_at)
    SELECT conversation_id, 'inbound', 'prospect', subject, body,
           category, round(confidence, 2), ext_id, now()
    FROM v
    ON CONFLICT (external_message_id) WHERE external_message_id IS NOT NULL
        DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
),
-- 1. Suppress. Before anything else, and whatever the category said.
sup AS (
    -- Both addresses: the one that asked to stop, and the one we wrote to.
    -- They are usually the same. When they are not, it is because the message
    -- was forwarded and a colleague answered "stop" - and suppressing only the
    -- colleague would leave the original recipient in the follow-up queue,
    -- which is the exact outcome the request was meant to prevent.
    INSERT INTO suppression_list (email, reason, note)
    SELECT addr, 'unsubscribe_request',
           'WF-08 ' || v.category || ': ' || left(v.reason, 180)
    FROM v
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (v.from_email), (lower(v.lead_email))) AS a(addr)
    WHERE v.is_stop AND addr IS NOT NULL AND addr <> ''
    ON CONFLICT (email) WHERE email IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
),
-- 2. Cancel everything not yet out of the door. 'cancelled' is not one of the
--    statuses the suppression trigger guards, so this cannot deadlock against
--    the row just inserted above.
cancelled AS (
    UPDATE outreach o
    SET status = 'cancelled',
        rejection_reason = 'cancelled by WF-08: recipient asked to stop'
    WHERE o.lead_id = (SELECT lead_id FROM v)
      AND o.status IN ('draft', 'pending_approval', 'approved', 'queued')
      AND (SELECT is_stop FROM v)
    RETURNING o.id
),
-- The message that was replied to, for the record.
replied AS (
    UPDATE outreach o
    SET reply_at = now()
    WHERE o.lead_id = (SELECT lead_id FROM v)
      AND o.status = 'sent'
      AND o.reply_at IS NULL
    RETURNING o.id
),
-- 3. The thread and the lead.
conv AS (
    UPDATE conversations cv
    SET status = CASE
            WHEN (SELECT is_stop FROM v)                        THEN 'unsubscribed'
            WHEN (SELECT low_conf OR human_required FROM v)     THEN 'awaiting_human'
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'NEGATIVE'          THEN 'closed_lost'
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'NOT_NOW'           THEN 'nurture'
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'OUT_OF_SCOPE'      THEN cv.status
            -- POSITIVE, QUESTION, PRICE and REFERRAL all stop here: WF-09 does
            -- not exist, so there is nothing that could answer them.
            ELSE 'awaiting_human'
        END,
        escalation_reason = CASE
            WHEN (SELECT low_conf FROM v) THEN 'classifier confidence '
                || (SELECT round(confidence, 2) FROM v)::text
                || ' after ' || CASE WHEN (SELECT escalated FROM v) THEN 'escalation' ELSE 'first pass' END
            WHEN (SELECT human_required FROM v) THEN left((SELECT reason FROM v), 200)
            ELSE cv.escalation_reason
        END,
        last_message_at = now()
    WHERE cv.id = (SELECT conversation_id FROM v)
    RETURNING cv.id, cv.status
),
lead AS (
    UPDATE leads l
    SET status = CASE
            WHEN (SELECT is_stop FROM v)                   THEN 'suppressed'
            -- A lead the operator has moved to a sales stage stays there: a question
            -- from a client at the proposal stage is still a proposal, and
            -- only he moves it on or marks it lost (0026_first_revenue.sql).
            WHEN l.status IN ('meeting', 'audit', 'proposal', 'closed_won') THEN l.status
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'POSITIVE'     THEN 'opportunity'
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'NEGATIVE'     THEN 'closed_lost'
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'NOT_NOW'      THEN 'nurture'
            WHEN (SELECT category FROM v) = 'OUT_OF_SCOPE' THEN l.status
            ELSE 'replied'
        END
    WHERE l.id = (SELECT lead_id FROM v)
    RETURNING l.id, l.status
),
-- 4. Tell a human, when there is something worth waking up for.
alert AS (
    SELECT q.notification_id
    FROM v
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL queue_notification(
        CASE WHEN v.category = 'POSITIVE' AND NOT v.is_stop
             THEN 'positive_reply' ELSE 'conversation_escalated' END,
        'reply:' || (SELECT conversation_id FROM v)::text || ':' || COALESCE(v.ext_id, v.category),
        CASE WHEN v.is_stop THEN 'Opt-out: ' ELSE v.category || ': ' END
            || COALESCE((SELECT j ->> 'company_name' FROM p), 'unknown'),
        'From: ' || v.from_email
            || E'\n' || 'Category: ' || v.category
            || ' (confidence ' || round(v.confidence, 2)::text
            || CASE WHEN v.escalated THEN ', escalated' ELSE '' END || ')'
            || E'\n' || 'Why: ' || left(v.reason, 200)
            || CASE WHEN v.is_stop
                    THEN E'\n\n' || 'Suppressed. Unsent messages cancelled. Do not reply.'
                    ELSE '' END
            || CASE WHEN v.timeline IS NOT NULL AND v.timeline <> ''
                    THEN E'\n' || 'Timeline: ' || v.timeline ELSE '' END
            || E'\n\n' || left(v.body, 1200),
        CASE WHEN v.category = 'POSITIVE' OR v.is_stop THEN 'immediate' ELSE 'normal' END,
        jsonb_build_object('conversation_id', v.conversation_id, 'category', v.category,
                           'confidence', v.confidence, 'escalated', v.escalated),
        NULL::uuid,
        v.lead_id,
        interval '7 days'
    ) q
    -- Nothing to say about an auto-reply that was already filtered, or a
    -- classification that changed nothing.
    WHERE v.category <> 'OUT_OF_SCOPE' OR v.is_stop OR v.human_required
)
SELECT (SELECT category FROM v)                 AS category,
       (SELECT round(confidence,2) FROM v)      AS confidence,
       (SELECT is_stop FROM v)                  AS suppressed,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM msg)::int          AS messages_written,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM sup)::int          AS suppressions_added,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM cancelled)::int    AS outreach_cancelled,
       (SELECT status FROM conv)                AS conversation_status,
       (SELECT status FROM lead)                AS lead_status,
       (SELECT notification_id FROM alert)      AS notification_id,
       -- For the reply draft (0028_reply_draft.sql).
       (SELECT lead_id FROM v)                  AS lead_id,
       (SELECT conversation_id FROM v)          AS conversation_id,
       (SELECT ext_id FROM v)                   AS external_message_id,
       (SELECT from_email FROM v)               AS from_email;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ conversation_id: $json.conversation_id, lead_id: $json.lead_id, external_message_id: $json.external_message_id, subject: $json.subject, body: $json.body, from_email: $json.from_email, lead_email: ($json.lead_email ?? ''), company_name: $json.company_name, classification: $json.classification, escalated: $json.escalated } ) }}

nodes.name: Apply Classification
nodes.notes: Suppression first, whatever the category said.

parameters.query:
-- Mail that will not be classified: an auto-reply, a bounce, or something that
-- belongs to no thread we started.
--
-- docs/workflows.md: "An unmatched message is stored and flagged for a human
-- rather than discarded." It cannot be stored in `messages`, which requires a
-- conversation, so the flag is a notification and the mail stays in the
-- mailbox where a person can read it.
--
-- A bounce does more than get flagged: it suppresses. An address that hard
-- bounces is not going to start working, and continuing to send to it is what
-- damages a young domain's reputation.
WITH p AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j),
c AS (
    SELECT lower(j ->> 'from_email')      AS from_email,
           j ->> 'subject'                AS subject,
           j ->> 'body'                   AS body,
           (j ->> 'is_auto_reply')::boolean AS is_auto_reply,
           (j ->> 'is_bounce')::boolean     AS is_bounce,
           (j ->> 'matched')::boolean       AS matched,
           NULLIF(j ->> 'lead_email', '')   AS lead_email,
           COALESCE((j ->> 'bounce_hard')::boolean, true) AS bounce_hard,
           COALESCE(j -> 'bounced_emails', '[]'::jsonb)   AS bounced_emails
    FROM p
),
-- The bounced address is the one the report names, not the postmaster's who
-- sent it. Until 2026-09-29 only a DSN that happened to carry our Message-ID
-- suppressed anything, because the sender fallback never matches a mailer
-- daemon. A temporary (4.x.x) failure suppresses nothing.
targets AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT lower(x)::citext AS email
    FROM c, jsonb_array_elements_text(c.bounced_emails) x
    WHERE c.is_bounce AND c.bounce_hard
    UNION
    SELECT lower(lead_email)::citext FROM c
    WHERE c.is_bounce AND c.bounce_hard AND c.lead_email IS NOT NULL
),
bounce_sup AS (
    INSERT INTO suppression_list (email, reason, note)
    SELECT t.email, 'hard_bounce', 'WF-08: ' || left((SELECT subject FROM c), 180)
    FROM targets t
    ON CONFLICT (email) WHERE email IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING
    RETURNING id
),
bounced_people AS (
    UPDATE people SET email_status = 'bounced'
    WHERE email IN (SELECT email FROM targets)
    RETURNING id
),
bounced_outreach AS (
    UPDATE outreach o SET status = 'bounced'
    FROM leads l, people pe
    WHERE o.lead_id = l.id AND pe.id = l.person_id
      AND pe.email IN (SELECT email FROM targets)
      AND o.status = 'sent'
      AND o.sent_at > now() - interval '14 days'
    RETURNING o.id
),
alert AS (
    SELECT q.notification_id
    FROM c
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL queue_notification(
        'system',
        'inbox:' || CASE WHEN c.is_bounce THEN 'bounce' WHEN c.is_auto_reply THEN 'auto' ELSE 'unmatched' END
            || ':' || md5(c.from_email || coalesce(c.subject, '')),
        CASE WHEN c.is_bounce     THEN 'Bounce: '
             WHEN c.is_auto_reply THEN 'Auto-reply: '
             ELSE 'Unmatched mail: ' END || left(coalesce(c.subject, '(no subject)'), 80),
        'From: ' || c.from_email
            || CASE WHEN c.is_bounce AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM targets)
                    THEN E'\n' || 'Suppressed: ' || (SELECT string_agg(email::text, ', ') FROM targets)
                    WHEN c.is_bounce AND NOT c.bounce_hard THEN E'\n' || 'Temporary failure: nothing suppressed'
                    WHEN c.is_bounce THEN E'\n' || 'Bounced address not found in the report: check it by hand'
                    ELSE '' END
            || E'\n\n' || left(coalesce(c.body, ''), 600),
        CASE WHEN c.is_bounce THEN 'normal' ELSE 'batched' END,
        jsonb_build_object('from', c.from_email, 'matched', c.matched),
        NULL::uuid, NULL::uuid, interval '1 day'
    ) q
    -- An auto-reply on a thread we know about is noise; one from nowhere is at
    -- least worth a batched line.
    WHERE NOT (c.is_auto_reply AND c.matched)
)
SELECT (SELECT from_email FROM c)                 AS from_email,
       (SELECT is_bounce FROM c)                  AS bounce,
       (SELECT is_auto_reply FROM c)              AS auto_reply,
       (SELECT matched FROM c)                    AS matched,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM bounce_sup)::int     AS suppressions_added,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM bounced_outreach)::int AS outreach_bounced,
       (SELECT notification_id FROM alert)        AS notification_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ from_email: $json.from_email, subject: $json.subject, body: $json.body, is_auto_reply: $json.is_auto_reply, is_bounce: $json.is_bounce, matched: ($json.matched ?? false), lead_email: ($json.lead_email ?? ''), bounce_hard: $('Prepare Inbound').item.json.bounce_hard, bounced_emails: $('Prepare Inbound').item.json.bounced_emails } ) }}

parameters.query:
-- What the reply draft is written from: the company, what was sent, the
-- thread so far, and what research found (prompts/reply-draft.md).
SELECT co.name            AS company_name,
       co.domain::text    AS domain,
       co.country,
       co.segment,
       (SELECT r.output #>> '{analysis,company_summary}'
        FROM agent_runs r
        WHERE r.company_id = co.id AND r.agent_name = 'research' AND r.status = 'success'
        ORDER BY r.finished_at DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AS research_summary,
       COALESCE((SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('subject', o.subject, 'body', o.body, 'sent_at', o.sent_at)
                                 ORDER BY o.sequence_step)
                 FROM outreach o WHERE o.lead_id = l.id AND o.status = 'sent'), '[]'::json) AS sent,
       COALESCE((SELECT json_agg(json_build_object('direction', m.direction, 'body', left(m.body, 3000),
                                                   'at', COALESCE(m.sent_at, m.created_at))
                                 ORDER BY COALESCE(m.sent_at, m.created_at))
                 FROM messages m
                 WHERE m.conversation_id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'conversation_id')::uuid), '[]'::json) AS thread
FROM leads l
JOIN companies co ON co.id = l.company_id
WHERE l.id = ($1::jsonb ->> 'lead_id')::uuid

-- The draft as its own Telegram message, after the classification alert. A
-- model that failed or returned nothing queues nothing: the alert already told
-- the operator there is a reply to answer.
SELECT q.notification_id
FROM (SELECT $1::jsonb AS j) p
CROSS JOIN LATERAL queue_notification(
    'reply_draft',
    'reply_draft:' || (j ->> 'conversation_id') || ':' || COALESCE(j ->> 'external_message_id', ''),
    'Predlog odgovora: ' || (j ->> 'company_name'),
    'Odgovor na: ' || (j ->> 'from_email') || ' (' || (j ->> 'category') || ')'
        || E'\n' || 'Kopiraj u Gmail i odgovori u istom threadu. Ništa nije poslato.'
        || E'\n\n' || (j ->> 'draft'),
    'immediate',
    jsonb_build_object('conversation_id', j ->> 'conversation_id', 'category', j ->> 'category'),
    NULL::uuid,
    (j ->> 'lead_id')::uuid,
    interval '7 days'
) q
WHERE btrim(COALESCE(j ->> 'draft', '')) <> ''

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ conversation_id: $('Apply Classification').item.json.conversation_id, external_message_id: $('Apply Classification').item.json.external_message_id, from_email: $('Apply Classification').item.json.from_email, category: $('Apply Classification').item.json.category, lead_id: $('Apply Classification').item.json.lead_id, company_name: $('Reply Context').item.json.company_name, draft: String(($json.message && $json.message.content) || '').replace(/<think>[\s\S]*?<\/think>/g, '').trim().slice(0, 3000) }) }}
